editorialRules: The biblical anchors are research moments, not yet approved scene count or final script chapters.
Chronology follows Bible/salvation history for biblical arc, 1962 Mass for liturgical arc.
Exactly one canonical Mass explanation owner per source-first prayer section; multiple Scriptural/mystagogical links allowed.
Existing 422 historical evidence claim IDs are preserved as links, not treated as 422 unique commentaries.
Every relationship type must distinguish direct liturgical words, adapted words, actual named figure, doctrinal typology, historical hypothesis and attributed meditation.
Dujardin headings remain his, not those of St Alphonsus; optional allegories never define 1962 historical origins.
Scripture expansion must delegate to shared Canonical Bible reader, and images to canonical approved artworks.
Do not project any research copy into LIVE Mass rubric/action rail without separate audit.

For every liturgical owner, carry independently classified MB passage links even when no full biblical chronology scene is assigned. Variable Proper readings are resolved from the Mass calendar/Proper rather than a guessed fixed chapter.

liturgicalChronology.title: Agnus Dei

biblicalCorrespondences.interpretiveQuestion: Explain the Paschal lamb's blood and shared meal as preparation for understanding Christ's sacrifice and the invocation Agnus Dei.
Explore substitution, willing suffering and the need to interpret sacrifice through Christ, not merely animal ritual.
Why is the same Lamb invoked before Communion and shown to the faithful?

editorialCautions: Do not assert the entire Roman Agnus Dei text is transcribed from Exodus.
Use controlled doctrinal sources for Eucharistic presence of once-for-all sacrifice; not mere pictorial analogy.
Mass Agnus Dei petitions are liturgical adaptation; distinguish Requiem form.

liturgicalChronology.title: Communion of the Faithful

biblicalCorrespondences.interpretiveQuestion: Distinguish bread that preserves temporal life from the Eucharistic Bread of Life, without collapsing manna into a literal Eucharist.
Join Bread of Life doctrine to actual Communion and centurion's humility without conflating the centurion's servant with the communicant's soul.
Distinguish the Canon's explicit remembrance of Resurrection from later meditation on Eucharistic recognition at Emmaus.
How does the Spirit-formed Church participate in Christ's sacrificial worship and communion of saints?
How does Eucharistic worship participate in the worship of the Lamb while sacramental signs anticipate the unveiled eternal communion?

editorialCautions: Matthew 8:8 speaks of the servant; liturgy changes to anima mea.
Priest and faithful have separate liturgical Domine non sum dignus contexts.
Emmaus does not independently prove that the breaking of bread in that episode is the Mass rite.
Pentecost cannot be used to prove arbitrary late rituals' apostolic origins.
Distinguish prophetic vision and future consummation from past-event timeline.
Do not depict angel physically lifting consecrated species into heaven.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Preparation
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Meditation preparation precedes the source-owned Mass Order; must not force C0001 as its historical origin.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: The beginning of Mass
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: The entry into the Mass is the textual location; Fall narrative is Dujardin's contemplation only.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Kyrie eleison
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Kyrie is present; expectation of the Messiah is not literal Kyrie text.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Gloria
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Only the opening Gloria wording is Luke 2; rest of hymn has separate history.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Prayer / Collect
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Collect text changes by feast/date; Christ's hidden life is Dujardin's meditation, not each Collect's Scripture.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Epistle
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Actual Epistle passage must come from resolved 1962 Proper, not Dujardin's precursor allegory.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Gospel
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Actual Gospel passage must come from resolved 1962 Proper; Dujardin's general ministry is thematic.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Credo
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Credo is fixed doctrinal formulation, not one geographically located biblical event.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Offertory
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Offertory is an anchor for meditation on Last Supper, not historically the Last Supper's bread action.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Lavabo
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Lavabo is a Psalm and practical handwashing; John 13 is solely a named devotional meditation.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Orate fratres
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Orate fratres is fixed; no Bible event forced.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Preface
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Preface varies; author contemplates Christ's thanksgiving, not exact text of any day's Preface.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Memento for living
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Memento of living; Gethsemane and Christ's prayer are devotional parallels.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Hanc igitur
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Hanc igitur source phrase is fixed; Leviticus 1:4 comparison does not explain ritual origin.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Consecration
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Two actual consecrations, one and the same Sacrifice sacramentally present; not a second bloody execution.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Memento for dead
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Memento for dead source cue; Purgatory/limbus distinctions require doctrinal review.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Pater noster
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Lord's Prayer is direct Scripture; Dujardin's tomb meditation is a different relationship.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Pax Domini
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Pax Domini and commixture occur separately; Resurrection symbolism is only devotional.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Agnus Dei
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Agnus Dei from John 1, while Dujardin contemplates Communion.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Post-Communion
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Postcommunion prayers vary; Ascension and Cenacle are authorial contemplations.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Blessing
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: Final blessing is an Order anchor for Pentecost contemplation, not biblical origin of benediction.

dujardinSecondaryMethod.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
dujardinSecondaryMethod.heading: Last Gospel
dujardinSecondaryMethod.qualifiedBySource: John 1 is the usual Last Gospel in the source corpus; individual special Masses may replace or omit it.

deliberateExclusions.subject: Noah
deliberateExclusions.reason: Useful broader salvation-history context but no strong present direct 1962 Mass-prayer anchor; retain as expandable biblical context, not forced centerpiece.

deliberateExclusions.subject: Every single Passion gesture equals biblical action
deliberateExclusions.reason: Ferrer/Dujardin and attributed Francis de Sales can offer a source-labelled optional meditation; Guéranger, Le Brun and Gihr oppose artificial universal causal derivations.

unresolvedEvents.reason: Optional priest entrance/preparation before the first reader prayer: use pre-Mass event owner, not Introit as guaranteed text
Asperges/Vidi aquam is a distinct conditional pre-Mass rite; no automatic Mass 39-owner binding
Broad Post-Consecration Canon event spans Unde et memores, Supra quae, Supplices, and possibly other prayers: cannot infer one 14-Canon owner
Peace-prayer and Solemn Pax combines distinct texts/minister events; handoff between Libera/Pax and prayers-before-Communion needs exact cue mapping
Departure/post-Mass prayers are outside the fixed final Mass prayer or depend on observance
